title: Enhancing LLM-based Autonomous Driving Agents to Mitigate Perception Attacks

live_model.evidence: Sec. 6.1: 'evaluate the performance of three LLMs (GPT-4-turbo, Llama-3-8B, and Gemma-1.1-7B)'; Sec. 1: 'GPT-4 achieves 84.48% detection and 86.36% avoidance rate'

prompt.location: Sec. 4 (system prompt and chain-of-thought design), Appendix A (full scene description), Appendix B (DSL log example)
prompt.note: Full system prompt text not printed; snapshot not stated (paper dated 2024-09).

claim.location: Sec. 1 / Sec. 8 summary (3,300 adversarial scenes); per-attack rates in Table 3

data.source: Adversarial driving scenarios released at https://tinyurl.com/llm-ad-eva (CARLA)

notes: Temperature 0.3; long DSL scene descriptions per call.

resolution.plan: Only prompt snippets (Listings 6-9), the component description (Sec. 5.3) and one scene description (Appendix A) are printed; the full system prompt, the response format and the DSL-to-text scene template are not. Obtain them together with the 3,300 adversarial scene descriptions from the scenario release, then make one call per scene to gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 at temperature 0.3 and count the scenes whose response flags an inconsistency; compare with the 84.48% headline (Sec. 6.2 reports 83.27% = 2748/3300 for the same quantity).
resolution.approximation: If the release holds only CARLA scenario configurations, the scenes must be re-simulated with CARLA and HUDSON's log collector, which is outside a prompt-only re-run and would make the record ineligible; the paper's two detection figures (84.48 vs 83.27) disagree.
